question: The new criminal laws aim to replace British-era laws with a focus on:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice delivery and citizen rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The new criminal laws in India aim to replace British-era laws with a focus on **ensuring justice delivery and safeguarding citizen rights**.
 
• These reforms emphasize modernizing the legal framework to address contemporary challenges and align with **India’s democratic ethos**.
 
• The laws aim to eliminate colonial legacies that were primarily designed to **suppress dissent** and control the population.
 
• Provisions are being introduced to ensure **speedy trials, victim-centric justice**, and a robust rights-based framework.
 
• The reforms are part of efforts to establish a justice system that reflects **India’s constitutional values** and promotes fairness, equality, and transparency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **British-era criminal laws:**

 
 
• The Indian Penal Code (IPC), Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), and Indian Evidence Act were introduced during colonial rule, primarily to serve the interests of the British Empire.
 
• The IPC was drafted in 1860 by Lord Macaulay, reflecting a colonial mindset.
 
• These laws were criticized for being outdated and not aligned with **modern democratic principles**.
 
 
 
• **Citizen rights focus:**
 
 
• The new laws aim to strengthen **fundamental rights** enshrined in the Indian Constitution, such as the right to equality, freedom, and life.
 
• They also emphasize **victim protection** and ensuring accountability of law enforcement agencies.
 
 
 
• **Key objectives of reforms:**
 
 
• Ensuring **timely delivery of justice** through simplified and efficient legal processes.
 
• Promoting **fair trials** and reducing delays in the judicial system.
 
 
 
• **Victim-centric approach:**
 
 
• Provisions for enhanced rights and compensation for victims of crimes.
 
• Special focus on crimes against women, children, and marginalized groups.
 
 
 
• **Modernization of laws:**
 
 
• Incorporating provisions to address **emerging crimes**, such as cybercrimes and financial frauds.
 
• Ensuring alignment with international human rights standards and treaties.
